html:
After the fall of Carthage in 146 BCE, Rome made northern Tunisia its province of Africa. For five centuries it was one of the main sources of grain and olive oil for the city of Rome.

Huge estates, many owned by the emperors, grew wheat in the valleys of the north, which was shipped from Carthage to feed the free grain of Rome, along with grain from Egypt. In the drier south, olive groves spread, and African oil was sold all over the empire in clay jars.

The wealth built towns full of temples, baths and mosaics, such as Dougga and El Jem. The province produced Christian leaders such as Tertullian and Augustine. The Vandals took it in 439, cutting Rome off from its bread basket.
sum: After the fall of Carthage in 146 BCE, Rome made northern Tunisia its province of Africa. For five centuries it was one of the main sources of grain and olive oil for the city of Rome.
